subject: Proposal: AB rollout guardrails + automated revert for Peridot (SLA mitigation)
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@peridot.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@peridot.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency during recent AB test - need rollback safety

Marcus —

Quick note from our SRE team: during the AB rollout you ran last night we saw 3x P99 tail latency for a subset of production requests that include long-context chat flows. That spike started at ~01:10 UTC and lasted ~12 minutes (see attached telemetry snapshot). It triggered downstream timeouts and two customer incidents.

We appreciate the gradual rollout, but we need stronger automatic mitigation to meet our contractual 99.9% uptime/latency SLA while you run experimental models. Specifically, can Redwood enable an automatic revert/pin to the previous model variant the instant P99 exceeds 1.5x baseline for more than a rolling 2-minute window? We also want an explicit durability pin so traffic doesn't flip back until we've manually greenlit the new variant.

Peridot contact: Asha Rao (ops). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Ops, Peridot AI

Attachment: peridot-sla-telemetry-snapshot.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@peridot.ai>, ops@peridot.ai
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency during recent AB test - need rollback safety

Hi Asha — thank you for the data and flagging the customer impact. Sorry you hit that during the AB run. We dug into the telemetry and saw the same spike; appears correlated with long-token sequences and a particular quantized variant we pushed into the B cohort.

High-level take: we can enable a short-circuit automatic revert policy (we call it "guardrail auto-revert") tied to the P99 threshold and a rolling window. A spec and proposed parameters are attached (redwood-proposed-ab-guardrails-v1.pdf). Proposed defaults for Peridot to satisfy your SLA:

- Trigger: P99 > 1.5x baseline for 120s continuous window (rolling 30s checks)
- Action: immediate traffic re-route to last pinned stable model for that route (no vote required)
- Pin duration: 4 hours by default (manual unpin required to re-open canary), with a safety override for mission-critical incidents
- Telemetry: automated incident note + trace to Peridot SRE channel and automatic snapshot upload

Operational notes: this will add an exception to the standard rollout policy (we'll record in the rollout config for audit). We need internal approval from Product and Platform to enable the automatic revert + manual pin duration > 1 hour because it changes rollback semantics.

I'll schedule a short sync with Lauren and Jordan to get product/ops approval and document the exact config. If Peridot wants a shorter pin or different thresholds we can iterate — but the 4-hour pin is conservative to prevent flip-flopping during follow-up investigations.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposed-ab-guardrails-v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency during recent AB test - need rollback safety

Folks — quick internal: I read Marcus's proposal. From a product/risk perspective I support enabling the guardrail auto-revert for Peridot as an SLA mitigation, but request the following modifications before we flip it on:

- Make the pin duration configurable per-account; for Peridot set initial pin to 2 hours (not 4) with escalation to 8 hours if SRE requests it.
- Add a cooldown that prevents immediate re-canary to the same variant for 24 hours unless manually authorized by the CE and SE leads.
- Ensure the auto-revert is accompanied by a read-only snapshot of the exact model binary hash + config sent to Peridot's audit log.

Jordan/Dylan: can you confirm runtime feasibility? Specifically I want to know whether we can atomically switch traffic and ensure KV cache compatibility when pinning to the older variant (long-context KV state). If that's risky we need a graceful in-place fallback that preserves user sessions.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

On Sun, Jun 14, 2026 at 09:05, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (quoted) "Hi Asha — thank you..."

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency during recent AB test - need rollback safety

Lauren — fast follow on feasibility: yes, we can do an atomic traffic switch at the routing layer to the pinned variant with these caveats:

- KV cache mismatch: if the pinned variant uses a different tokenizer/kv-layout we may see a short cold-KV penalty for affected sessions. We can mitigate by routing existing session tokens to a degraded path for a short time while warming the cache asynchronously. That will keep per-request latency within the SLA but may temporarily increase token CPU for those sessions.
- We will implement a 30s precondition check that validates the pinned model is load-ready on all regional nodes before cutting traffic. If any node fails the precondition, the auto-revert will abort and raise an immediate escalation to Platform.
- Implementing the 24h re-canary cooldown is straightforward — we'll add a per-route cooldown flag in rollout metadata.

I recommend we: (1) agree thresholds with Peridot; (2) apply a Peridot-specific guardrail policy in their dedicated config; (3) run a 48-hour supervised canary with the guardrail enabled in a staging-like small percentage before flipping to full auto-revert in production.

Jordan Blake
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
